title: In four adult fly connectomes, synapse-count differences of strong connections after neuron gains are specific to each map; no detectable part is shared by the two TEM maps or the two FIB-SEM maps
abstract: Question: prior studies found that synapse-count differences between adult fly connectomes repeat on both sides of the brain after neuron gains are removed, but could not separate biology from shared reconstruction effects. Approach: we added the hemibrain as a fourth animal. FAFB and BANC use TEM; the male CNS and the hemibrain use FIB-SEM and FlyEM reconstruction. For 5,951 strong ipsilateral connections between 1,039 cell types with one neuron per side, we removed one input and one output gain per neuron in each of seven copies (two sides of three maps, right side of the hemibrain). Covariances of differences from four different animals (tetrads) are free of Poisson noise and of effects of any single map. Results: the family tetrad was -0.010 log-count units squared (95% identity-bootstrap interval -0.024 to 0.003), -6% (-15% to +2%) of the FAFB versus male CNS excess over Poisson. A left-right asymmetry common to all animals was 0.0001 (-0.004 to 0.004). Each map had its own component that repeats on both sides: 0.022 (FAFB), 0.036 (male CNS) and 0.151 (BANC). It stayed when the synapse table changed and was spread over most cell types. The remaining part, specific to one side of one map, was 71% of the FAFB versus male CNS excess. Thus the bilateral component of between-animal differences is a property of each map, not of its imaging family. Limitations: four animals and one male; one factor groups imaging, segmentation and synapse detection; the hemibrain has one side; only strong connections of one-per-side types; individual biology and map-specific reconstruction remain confounded.
